full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioners is that he applied to the respondent No.2 bank for a loan of Taka 50,00.000 and he, having deposited the margin amount of Taka 15,00,000 was granted in his favour and as security of the above loan, the petitioner made equitable mortgage of his properties and though he made substantial payment the respondent No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1993 praying for realisation of Taka 61,69,201 by sale of the mortgaged properties and on.3 1-8-1997 prelim in any decree was passed ordering that in default of the payment of the aforesaid amount of Taka 61,69,201 with interest etc in terms of preliminary, decree final decree was passed on 9-7-1998 and then to enforce the same the respondent No. 2 filed Title Execution Case No. 59 of 1998 praying for, realisation of the decretal amount with cost, interest etc by sale, of the mortgaged properties and subsequently, at the prayer of the respondent No. 2 the Court below attached the properties mortgaged by the petitioner and fixed the date of auction on 2-3-2000 for sale of the attached properties. However, by order dated 19-2-2000 passed in Miscellaneous ease No. 14 of 2000, which was started on the basis of an application filed under Order XXI rule 58 filed by one Rowshan Ara, who claimed ownership on the mortgaged properties, further proceeding of the above execution case Was stayed till disposal of the aforesaid miscellaneous case. Then on 31-3-2003 the aforesaid Miscellaneous case was taken up for hearing and Rowshan Ara, the petitioner of the above Miscellaneous case having not been found on call, the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default. However in the meantime, on 25-3-2003, on the basis of the application filed by the respondent No.2 under Order XLI, rule 37 Cl'C Annexure-D, praying for issuance of warrant of arrest, against' the petitioner/judgment-debtor, the impugned order, Annexure-D(1), was passed. 

 4. Mr Md Idrisur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in the instant case decree was passed for realisation of Taka 61,69,201 along with interest cost etc by way of selling the mortgaged properties and then application for execution was filed under Order XXI, rule 11 (2)CC seeking the assistance of Court only for sale of the mortgaged properties and not for arrest and detention of the petitioner/judgment- debtor in civil prison and moreover, in terms of the provisions of the proviso to section 51 CPC no opportunity was given to the judgment-debtor for showing cause as to why he should not be. committed to civil prison and further in terms of the provisions of Order XXI, rule 37 CPC no notice was given to the judgment-debtor/petitioner asking him to appear before the Court and as held in the case of Antibiotic Stores and others vs Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Ada/at and others, 55 DLR (AD) 13, in execution proceeding pending before the Artha Rin Adalat, provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable and accordingly, the impugned order; having been passed without complying the specific provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure will be applicable and accordingly, the impugned order, having been passed without complying the specific provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure cannot be sustained and the principle laid down in 54 DLR 78 is not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case. 

 5. Mr Md Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent No. 2, submits that due to conspiracy of the petitioner/judgment-debtor no bidder turned up on the date fixed for auction and the judgment-debtor/petitioner, with malafide intention, pushed forward his sister Raushan Ara to file the above Miscellaneous Case. No. 24 of 2000 and obtained the order of stay. Further, in terms of Order XXI, rule 30 CPC decree having been passed for payment of money, the Court was to pass order for issuing Civil Warrant for arrest of the judgment- debtor and accordingly, the respondent No. 2 filed application dated 25-2-2003 under Order XXI, rule 37 CPC Annexure-D, in terms of which the impugned order WIlS passed and in the case of Hazera Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat 54 DLR 78 it has been held that under section 6(Ka) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990, as amended, the Artha Rin Adalat has power to pass order for arrest of even a women in execution of a decree for payment of money in spite of the provisions of section 56 CPC which bars issuing order of arrest or detention in the civil prison of a woman in execution of a decree for payment of money and accordingly, since under the above section 6(Ka), Artha Rin Adalat has been given the power even to pass an order which may not be in conformity with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure relating to the execution of a decree, no interference with the impugned order is called for. 

 8. From the contents of the applications dated 25-3-2003 Annexure-D, it appears that respondent No.2 Bank filed the present execution case for realisation of Taka 96, 61,374 as on 20-8-1998 with 18% compensation and in the aforesaid application they took the stand that decree was to be executed by way of attachment and sale of the mortgaged properties and also by putting the petitioner/ judgment-debtor in civil prison. 

 11. In the case of Antibiotic Stores & others vs Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat and others 55 DLR (AD) 13, the Appellate Division held that under section 5(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, Artha Rin Adalat is it Civil Court having all the powers and jurisdiction under the Civil Procedure Code subject to the provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and since the impugned order in question was passed in execution proceeding of the Artha Rin Adalat, the provisions of Code of Civil Procedure should be followed and accordingly, instead of invoking writ jurisdiction it was the duty of the petitioner to avail the procedure laid down in Order XXI, rule 90 CPC in setting aside the auction sale. 

 12. In the case of Sultana Jute Mills Limited vs Agrani Bank, 46 DLR (AD) 174, the Appellate Division observed as follows: 

 13. In the case of Islami Bank Bangladesh vs Md Shajuddin 52 DLR (AD) 76 it has been held that there being no provision in the Artha Rin contrary to the provision of Order IX, rule 9 CPC Artha Rin Adalat may pass an order restoring a suit which was dismissed for default. 

 16. It appears that previously in terms of the provisions of rules 5 to 9 of Order XXI CPC a decree passed. by Artha Rin Adalat had to be transferred to executing Court for execution and as it will appear from the proviso to Order XXI, rule 37 CPC quoted earlier, complication could also arise if the judgment-debtor left the jurisdiction of the executing Court and as it appears it is only to avoid such situation that section 6(Ka) was incorporated in Artha Rin Adalat Ain which gave the Artha Rin Adalat the power to execute the decree passed by it and as it appears the above provision cannot be stretched to imply that in execution cases pending in Artha Rin Adalat the provisions of section 51 and/or Order XXI, rule 37 regarding issue of show cause and other notice etc have been waived.
